_note: 行事の食（年中行事）の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/seasonal/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/events-kids-minor-2026-10-10.md と各系譜ページの sources。正月・節分・ひな祭りの3本を published。端午・七夕/お盆・十五夜・冬至・大晦日・クリスマスは planned（era は「—」）。雑煮・餅・赤飯は rice-sides、年越しそばはそば、七夕・お盆のそうめんは somen 側で扱う。彼岸・七五三・重陽はメモの素材が名称程度なので行を作っていない
name: Food for annual events

origin.era: Osechi's basic form late Edo; seven-herb porridge Muromachi to Edo

cells.when: The New Year days; seven-herb porridge on 7 January
cells.food: Osechi with three iwai-zakana (black beans, tazukuri, herring roe); rice porridge with seven spring herbs
cells.meaning: A wish for each dish (health, harvest, children, luck); the herbs’ vigour for a long life

lineages.name: Setsubun
lineages.nameJa: 節分（豆まき・いわし・恵方巻）

origin.place: Nationwide; ehōmaki told as an Osaka custom
origin.era: Bean-throwing said to begin in the Muromachi period; ehōmaki national from the 1990s

cells.when: Around 3 February, the day before the start of spring
cells.food: Roasted soybeans, grilled sardines, the sushi roll called ehōmaki
cells.meaning: Driving out evil and wishing for good health; ehōmaki eaten facing the year’s lucky direction
cells.varies: Sardines mainly in western Japan; peanuts in parts of Hokkaido; konnyaku or oden in Sorachi

origin.era: Doll display for girls from the Edo period

cells.food: Chirashi-zushi, clam soup, three-coloured diamond mochi, white sake or amazake, hina-arare
cells.meaning: A girl’s growth; clams for a well-matched marriage; the mochi’s colours for spring
cells.varies: Hina-arare round and salty in Kansai, rice-shaped and sweet in Kanto

cells.when: 5 May; old-calendar 5 June in eastern Shimane
cells.meaning: Kashiwa-mochi for life passing from parent to child; chimaki to ward off evil
cells.varies: Eastern Shimane wraps rice-flour dumplings in bamboo leaves; called maki or kayamaki in Oki

cells.food: Sōmen at both; Buddhist shōjin meals and dumplings at Obon
cells.meaning: Different stories for the same noodles; for Obon, the reins of the ancestors’ horse
cells.varies: Obon foods differ by region (zunda mochi in Miyagi, bon-jiru in Matsusaka, kainoko-jiru in Kagoshima)

cells.when: Full moon of the old eighth month (mid-September to early October)
cells.meaning: Thanks for the harvest and a wish for the next
cells.varies: Slightly flattened in parts of Kanto; three-coloured in Nagoya; hollowed in Shizuoka; fuchagi in Okinawa

cells.meaning: Several given together: the n sound brings luck; it keeps and feeds you in winter
Three given together: a long life, cutting off the year’s troubles, good health
cells.varies: Names, the day it is eaten, the kind of soba and the broth differ by region
